text:
The low hum had started sometime in the early afternoon, a sound more felt than heard, like a distant engine perpetually idling beneath the town. David Vance ignored it at first, his gaze snagged on the faded photograph pinned to his corkboard – a local councillor, missing five years. But then the ripples in his cold coffee cup became too pronounced to dismiss, tiny concentric circles shivering across the dark surface, mirroring the faint tremor in the worn floorboards beneath his feet. It wasn't an earthquake, not in any sense Blackwood Bay usually knew, but a persistent, almost *insistent* vibration that seemed to emanate from the very bedrock.

He ran a hand over the rough grain of his oak desk, feeling the faint thrum against his palm. It was the kind of noise that didn't just rattle objects, it rattled the nerves, an invisible pressure pushing in from all sides. He’d lived long enough in Blackwood Bay to know that when the ground started to whisper, it usually wasn't telling bedtime stories. It felt like the town itself was clearing its throat, preparing to spit out another one of its ugly truths, a precursor to the real darkness that always seemed to follow the strange weather or the unsettling quiet.
